title: Everything I eat to get HUGE (Full Bulking Plan)
summary: NH walks through the bulking plan he has used for a year and a half: about 80% of calories from carbs (rice, bread, croissants), modest protein around 100 g/day mostly from fish and poultry, carb cycling by training day, heavy use of spices, water-only hydration and just three supplements (whey, creatine, MSM). He argues naturals should eat like normal people, cook for themselves and avoid extreme bro-diets.
claims: Training is the main driver of natural muscle growth; diet only fuels it, but a poor bulking plan wastes the effort
About 80% of his calories come from carbs; a past high-fat high-protein diet made him gain fat, feel sluggish, perform poorly and hurt his health
Sandwiches are underrated for bulking: cheap, quick and easy to load with calories via butter, peanut butter, honey or mayo
His breakfast is 3-4 microwaved croissants with jam and butter plus whey protein
White sticky rice is his staple: digests easily, is low in satiety so he can eat more, and fills glycogen for training
If you worry about insulin sensitivity, swap white rice for lower-glycemic carbs like brown rice, sweet potato, quinoa or lentils
Carb cycling: lots of carbs on upper-body days, fewer carbs and more animal protein on leg days, then eat the carbs the day after legs when hunger hits
He trains an upper/lower split six times a week with one rest day
On his weekly rest day he eats low or no carbs and fewer calories, so it is the only day not in a surplus
Carbs do not make you fat; processed low-fiber high-sugar products do because they are not satiating and keep you craving
Use whole fruit like bananas and apples as snacks instead of processed sweets: more fiber and micronutrients, more satiating
Roast sliced zucchini with olive oil and salt for an hour, or fry onions to mix into rice, for cheap tasty veggie sides
Ending the day with a salad with balsamic vinegar helps digestion when eating a lot
Eat more vegetables on a bulk than on a cut; bulking is not an excuse to skip them
He eats only about 100 g protein a day, roughly 0.5 g per lb at 215-220 lb, and still grows, so sees no reason to eat more
He limits canned tuna or salmon to twice a week because large predatory fish accumulate mercury; small fish like sardines are safer
He eats fatty fish like trout twice a week, pan-cooked to keep it juicy with crispy skin
He eats 4-6 eggs per week as a middle ground between people claiming one egg a day kills you and those eating 12 a day
Olive oil is the only oil he cooks with
Butter is the only dairy he eats, once or twice a week; fats come as a byproduct, though naturals need some fat for hormones
Have a go-to high-calorie meal you can produce at any moment; most people fail bulks because life gets in the way without one
He mostly stopped weekly meal prep because it wasted food that went stale; he cooks fresh but keeps a few precooked dishes in the fridge
Make your bulk a series of enjoyable rituals, like cooking while listening to podcasts, so you stick to it
Every man should learn to cook: it is cheaper and healthier than ordering food
Spices have no calories but make calorie-dense food far easier to eat; bland food does not make you hardcore
Season chicken with poultry seasoning and bake 25-35 minutes; garlic and onion powder go on anything
He uses Mexican worm salt (sal de gusano) on nearly every dish instead of plain sea salt
Hydration is rarely discussed but poor hydration hurts performance, recovery and health
He drinks only carbon-filtered water: no coffee, tea or soda
Alcohol is the worst drink for performance; a binge wrecks the next day's training
People who train, sweat and cook their own food are likely low in salt and should add it rather than fear it
After a big meal he drinks 1 L of water with a whole lemon squeezed in before bed to ease digestion
Supplements are the least important part of a bulk; they do almost nothing compared with food
He takes one scoop of whey a day, sometimes 3-4 times a week; if shakes are most of your protein you are bulking wrong
He takes creatine daily without cycling, above the label dose, for work capacity; stop it if it causes hair loss
He has taken MSM powder nonstop for 5 years for knees he hurt long ago; it was the only thing that worked, tastes awful, and boosts hair and nail growth
Any supplement that truly builds muscle is a steroid and will wreck your hormones
Pro bodybuilder bro-diets are theatrics; naturals copying them burn out, so eat like a normal person and avoid diets that ban whole food groups
Look at your ancestry to guess which foods suit you; descended from European peasants, he thrives on high carbs
The point of a bulk is to train hard and consistently; if the diet is painful you will not stick to it
